question: I have a level 8 bachelor's degree. How long can I stay on Stamp 1G
reference: 12 months. Only graduates who completed a master's (Level 9) can be given a further 12 months.
answer:
You can stay on Stamp 1G for 12 months, unless you completed a master’s degree programme, in which case you may be granted a further 12 months [1]. 

After the initial or extended period of 12 months, you must find a job that requires an employment permit and follow the usual application process with Department of Enterprise Trade and Employment [1].

question: Can I use the graduate programme again if I get another degree later
reference: Yes, a graduate who achieves a higher-level award (e.g. Level 9 or above) can re-enter the programme for another 12 months, subject to the overall eight-year limit, but nobody can access the programme on more than two separate occasions.
answer: Yes, you can re-enter the Third Level Graduate Programme for an additional period of 12 months if you achieve a higher level award, such as level 9 or above, after previously benefiting from the programme at a level 8 award or above [1]. However, this is subject to the overall limit of eight years and you must not have already exceeded two separate occasions of accessing the Programme [1].

reference: Yes. Periods spent on Stamp 1G as a graduate student count as reckonable residence for a citizenship/naturalisation application.

question: Can I start my own business while I am on Stamp 1G
reference: No. On Stamp 1G you may work full time but you are not permitted to operate a business or be self-employed.
answer: No, you are not permitted to operate a business or be self-employed while on a Stamp 1G [1]. This is also stated for spouses and de facto partners of CSEP holders and researchers on a Hosting Agreement permission [2].

question: How much does it cost to register my immigration permission
reference: The standard registration fee is EUR 300 (some permissions do not require a fee). It is paid by credit or debit card; cash is not accepted.
answer: The standard registration fee is €300 [2, 3]. You can pay this fee by credit or debit card only [4].

question: I am on Stamp 2 and my new course has not started yet. Can I renew my permission now
reference: No. Stamp 2 applicants (students) must wait until their course starts before they can apply to renew.
answer: No, you must wait until your course starts before applying to renew your IRP card [3].

question: Can I book my registration appointment before I arrive in Ireland
reference: No. You book after you arrive: when you enter Ireland your passport gets a landing stamp instructing you to register within 90 days, and appointments should only be booked after that instruction.
answer: No [2]. You should only book an appointment after you receive an instruction to register on arrival in the State, and your passport will be endorsed with a landing stamp instructing that you register within 90 days [3].

question: I am a visa-required national. Can I travel abroad before my first registration appointment
reference: If you leave the State before your registration appointment, you will not be able to re-enter without a new entry visa.
answer: No, if you are a visa-required national and leave the state prior to your registration appointment, you will not be able to re-enter the state without a new entry visa [2].

question: What is the difference in work rights between Stamp 2 and Stamp 1G
reference: Stamp 2: casual employment of up to 20 hours per week during term and 40 hours per week during holidays. Stamp 1G (graduate): you can work full time, but you may not operate a business or be self-employed.
answer:
Stamp 1G allows you to look for employment under the Third Level Graduate Programme, subject to conditions [1]. You can work full time in accordance with employment law requirements, but you are not permitted to operate a business or be self-employed [1]. This is different from Stamp 2, where your other permissions and conditions remain the same as for Stamp 2 while on a Stamp 1G [1].

Stamp 1G also allows spouses or de facto partners of CSEP holders or researchers on a Hosting Agreement to take up employment without needing an employment permit [2].

question: How many years in total can I study in Ireland on Stamp 2
answer: You can study English language courses for a maximum of three permissions of eight months each, which is a total of two years [2]. After that time, you must enrol on a higher education programme listed on the ILEP if you wish to remain as a student [2].

question: My internship is part of my course. Can I work more than 20 hours a week on it
reference: Yes, if the internship or placement forms an integral part of a course on the ILEP leading to a major award at NFQ Level 7 or above; students may then work more than 20 hours per week on that placement.
answer:
Yes, students enrolled on courses leading to major awards at NFQ Level 7 (or equivalent) and above may undertake an internship/placement where this forms an integral part of an academic course listed on the ILEP [1]. Students may work more than 20 hours per week in these placements/internships [1].

However, it's worth noting that higher education institutions must ensure that the placements are appropriate to the nature and level of the academic programme [1], and working hours and conditions must be in accordance with employment law provisions [2].

question: Do I need a two-year job contract to get a Critical Skills Employment Permit
reference: Yes. The permit is only issued for a job offer of at least 2 years. For shorter job offers, a General Employment Permit may be applied for instead.
answer: Yes, you need a 2-year job offer in respect of an eligible occupation from the prospective employer [5]. The employment permit will issue to the prospective employee (a certified copy will issue to the employer) for a job where there is a strategic skills shortage [3] and the remuneration requirement is met [4].

question: My job pays 70,000 euro but it is not on the Critical Skills Occupations List. Can I still get a Critical Skills permit
reference: Possibly. All occupations paying over EUR 68,911 are eligible, except those on the Ineligible List of Occupations or contrary to the public interest (and you need a 2-year job offer). A good answer explains this condition rather than giving a flat yes or no.
answer: No, you cannot get a Critical Skills Employment Permit if your occupation is not on the Critical Skills Occupations List [3]. The permit is only for occupations deemed critically important to growing Ireland's economy and in significant shortage of supply in our labour market [3].

question: Can my employer take the permit fee out of my salary
reference: No. Where the employer is the applicant, the employer may not make any deductions from the permit holder's pay, or recover from them any charge, fee or expense related to the application.
answer: According to [1], while the fee may be paid by a third party, current policy restricts refunds to applicants only. However, it also states that where the employer is the applicant, in accordance with section 55 of the Employment Permits Act 2024, the employer may not make any deductions from the remuneration of, or seek to recover from, the holder of the employment permit concerned any charge, fee or expense related to the application [1].

question: How long do I need to work on a General Employment Permit before I can get Stamp 4
reference: 57 months from commencement of employment in the State on a General Employment Permit (compared with 21 months for a Critical Skills Employment Permit).
answer: You must have been in employment in the State for a minimum of 57 months on the basis of a General Employment Permit [1, 2, 4].

question: What documents do I need to renew my permission online
reference: It depends on your stamp. Renewals generally need a copy of your current IRP card and the biometric page of your passport, plus the documents listed for your specific stamp category. A good answer explains that the list depends on the stamp or asks which one the person has.
answer:
To renew your Stamp 3 permission online, you will need to upload:
- The biometric page of your current valid passport(s) [2]
- Your permission letter from the Department of Justice that details the conditions under which you were granted a Stamp 3 [2]
- Your letter of sponsorship [2]

Note: You can find more information on required documents for online renewal in section "Online Renewal" of source [3].

question: Do I need private medical insurance to register
reference: For certain immigration permissions, yes: you must provide proof of appropriate private medical insurance. Whether you need it depends on your permission type.
answer: For certain immigration permissions, you will require valid private medical insurance with your application [1]. You must provide proof of holding the appropriate medical insurance when applying [2]. The required documents for registration and renewal include original documents including private medical insurance with the required cover, if applicable [4].
